answer: Because the vine height is fixed at intake and entered in the signal receipt, the pulse audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 768 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 9 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
